summary: This sermon makes the case for why Canvas Church has formal membership, arguing that in a culture that glamorizes independence, membership provides a practical framework to identify who is committed to doing life together as the local church. Using the image of living stones being built into a temple on the foundation of Christ, the pastor challenges listeners to consider how their lives and community might be different if they committed to a local body of believers rather than remaining isolated.
key_points: Culture glamorizes individualism, creating tension with church commitment
Membership distinguishes committed members from spiritual consumers and the spiritually curious
Church as living stones built together on Christ the cornerstone into a temple
Membership makes leadership harder but creates diverse, beautiful community
Committing to imperfect people is better than isolated independence
big_idea: Church membership is the practical way committed followers of Jesus identify themselves as living stones being built together on Christ's foundation into a temple that reveals God to the watching world.
title: POURED OUT: Why Church Membership?
